prioritization: Distinct upstream formulations first, occurrence count second, then stable canonical ID. Mathematical validity, source suitability, existing-meaning duplicates and provider conventions remain independent review requirements.

top_candidates.context: Category theory: ordinary category with objects, morphisms, identities and associative composition, without requiring its collection of objects to be a set; any size assumptions are stated separately.
Category theory: ordinary functor between arbitrary categories C and D without assuming smallness; object/arrow assignments preserve identities and compositions.

Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.

Set theory: preimage or inverse image of subset B⊆Y under an arbitrary function f:X→Y, defined as f^{-1}[B]={x∈X:f(x)∈B}; notation f^{-1}[B] never presupposes that f is invertible. Includes underlying set preimages of open/measurable sets and contractions of prime ideals under ring homomorphisms, where additional structure is a separate condition.

Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra R[X_i : i in I] over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, for an arbitrary set I of independent indeterminates; each polynomial has finite monomial support. Includes the one-variable and finite-variable cases and polynomial algebras over fields and quotient coefficient rings.

top_candidates.query: residue field of a local ring
top_candidates.context: Commutative algebra and algebraic geometry: residue field A/m of a commutative local ring (A,m), including the prime-localized κ(p)=R_p/pR_p and the scheme-point κ(s)=O_{S,s}/m_s.
Commutative algebra: associative commutative ring R with a specified multiplicative identity 1_R; the prime-ideal formulation does not assume the ring is an integral domain.
Module theory: free left R-module over a unital ring with an R-basis, equivalently a direct sum R^{(I)} of copies of R, possibly infinite rank.

Module theory: quotient left R-module M/N by an R-submodule N, whose elements are additive cosets m+N with addition and R-scalar action induced by M. Includes ideal modules I/I², successive filtration quotient modules and regular-module quotients R/I; extra ring, graded, flatness, or field structure is not part of this quotient-module meaning.
Set theory: injectivity of an arbitrary map f:X→Y, meaning f(x)=f(y) implies x=y for all x,y in X; for structured maps this is the underlying-set condition.

Set theory: surjective function f:X→Y whose image is the entire stated codomain Y; for module homomorphisms this is the underlying-set surjectivity of the R-linear map, independent of linearity, free domain, or choice of basis.
Category theory: f:X→Y is an isomorphism iff there exists g:Y→X with gf=id_X and fg=id_Y; no underlying-set bijectivity is assumed.

Commutative algebra: scalar extension of a commutative unital k-algebra R along field extension K/k, yielding the unital K-algebra R⊗_k K with induced multiplication (r⊗a)(s⊗b)=rs⊗ab and K-scalar structure.
Order theory: supremum sup(A) of subset A⊆S, an upper bound no greater than every other upper bound when it exists.
Category theory: hom-collection Hom_C(X,Y) of arrows X→Y; a preadditive category requires these collections to be sets carrying abelian group structures, without requiring all objects to form a set.

Polynomial algebra: a nonzero univariate polynomial f(X)=a_nX^n+⋯+a_0 over a commutative unital coefficient ring is monic if its leading coefficient a_n equals the multiplicative identity 1, including degree zero unit polynomial 1.
Algebraic geometry: distinguished principal open D(f)={p∈Spec(R):f∉p} of a commutative ring's affine spectrum.

Commutative algebra: product IJ of two ideals of a commutative unital ring R, generated by finite sums of pairwise products; ordinary ideal powers I^n for n≥1 by repeated ideal multiplication, and by convention I^0=R when nonnegative exponents are used.

Commutative algebra: kernel ideal of a unital homomorphism φ:A→B of commutative rings, consisting of all a∈A mapped to 0_B; for a polynomial evaluation map it is the ideal of polynomial relations, and for a quotient-localization composite it is the inverse image of zero in the target ring.

top_candidates.query: direct sum ⊕_i M_i of a family of modules
top_candidates.context: Module theory: direct sum ⊕_{i∈I} M_i of left R-modules, the module of families (m_i) of finite support with componentwise addition and scalar multiplication, distinct from their unrestricted product.
Set theory: binary intersection A∩U of two sets, whose elements belong to both A and U; applied to ambient open sets and a subspace.
Set theory: relative complement A\B={x∈A:x∉B} for two sets A,B⊆X; in the sigma-algebra axiom A,B are members of Σ.

top_candidates.query: commutative unital algebra over a field
top_candidates.context: Commutative algebra: commutative unital algebra A over a specified base field k, with a chosen unital structure homomorphism k→A; A need not be a field, a domain or geometrically regular.
Commutative algebra: principal ideal generated by one element

Set theory: bijective mapping f:X→Y, a function that is both injective and surjective onto the specified codomain Y; equivalently a function admitting a two-sided inverse Y→X. In structured settings this refers only to the underlying-set map, not to automatic continuity, R-linearity, group structure, or naturality.
